(2) Place names such as "LUGAL-u-te" (likely referring to the city of Nineveh), "URU LUGAL DINGIR-MEŠ" (the city of the king of the gods, likely Ashur), and "URU kiš-šu-te" (the city of Calah) suggest this inscription is from the Neo-Assyrian Empire, specifically during the reign of a king who ruled from these cities.

(4) The genre formulae used in the text, such as the description of building activities ("it-ta-bi a-na LUGAL-u-te"), suggest this is a building inscription or possibly an annalistic text detailing construction projects.
